blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: This one replaces all its Pods at once when the template changes.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to watch its updates.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web

blocks.title: Four copies and their label
blocks.what: Keep four Pods running, and manage the Pods labelled app: recreate-web.
blocks.why: Four copies make it easy to see them all stop together.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Four copies of the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: recreate-web

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. Changing it starts an update.
blocks.why: The update strategy decides how old Pods give way to new ones.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: recreate-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: recreate-web

blocks.title: A page that shows its version
blocks.what: busybox writes a page saying version, then serves it on port 80.
blocks.why: Reading the page shows which version a Pod runs.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: A small web server that shows its version
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: recreate-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: recreate-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]

blocks.title: The version number
blocks.what: VERSION is 1, and the command writes it into the page. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Changing VERSION changes the template, so it starts an update.
blocks.ifRemoved: The page says just version, with no number.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: recreate-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: recreate-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              value: "1"

blocks.title: Stop, then start
blocks.what: Recreate stops every old Pod before starting any new one.
blocks.why: Use it when two versions must never run together, such as an app that changes a database format.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses a rolling update, so old and new Pods run side by side for a while.
blocks.comment: Stop all old Pods before starting new ones
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: recreate-web
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: recreate-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: recreate-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo version $VERSION > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              value: "1"

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running: four.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is recreate-web.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: recreate-web, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Write a page saying version and $VERSION, then serve it on port 80.
notes.spec.strategy: How the Deployment replaces old Pods with new ones when the template changes.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].na: VERSION, which the command writes into the page.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].va: Version 1. Quotes keep the number as text, as env values must be.
notes.spec.strategy.type: Recreate: stop all old Pods, then start the new ones. The app is down in between.

tryIt.result: Prints successfully rolled out once all four Pods are running.
Changes the template, which starts the update.
Waits about 30 seconds while the old Pods stop, then the new ones start. No Pod serves meanwhile.
Events show the old set scaled from 4 to 0, then the new set from 0 to 4.

check.pattern: Scaled down replica set recreate-web-\S+ from 4 to 0[\s\S]*Scaled up replica set recreate-web-\S+ from 0 to 4

tryIt.result: Removes the Deployment and its Pods.

questions.question: During an update, how many Pods serve the page?
questions.explain: All old Pods stop before any new one starts. The app is down in between.

questions.question: When is Recreate the right choice?
answers: When two versions must never run at the same time
questions.explain: Recreate trades downtime for never mixing versions.

questions.question: Why did the old Pods take about 30 seconds to stop?
answers: busybox’s web server ignores the stop signal, so the grace period runs out
questions.explain: The default grace period is 30 seconds, as the timing lesson showed.

fix.message: The Deployment "recreate-web" is invalid: spec.strategy: Unsupported value: {"Type":"recreate","RollingUpdate":null}: supported values: "Recreate", "RollingUpdate"
fix.explain: Strategy names are case-sensitive. Kubernetes knows Recreate and RollingUpdate only.
fix.fix: Write the strategy with a capital R: Recreate.
